Direct answer

What this STL viewer does

This is a free online STL viewer that reads ASCII and binary STL files directly in your browser. Use it to view STL online when you want a quick visual check: it renders a WebGL preview, reports the X × Y × Z bounding box, triangle count, file size and detected format, and lets you switch between Z-up and Y-up. Your STL is never uploaded, stored or sent to a server.

Whether you call it an STL viewer online, online STL viewer, STL file viewer, free STL viewer, STL opener or STL reader, this is the same browser-only tool.

How to use this STL file viewer

  1. 1

    Open the viewer

    Open the free STL viewer on this page. It runs locally in your browser.

  2. 2

    Choose or drop your STL

    Click Choose STL file or drag an ASCII or binary .stl file onto the drop zone.

  3. 3

    Inspect the preview

    Orbit the WebGL preview, toggle wireframe or grid, and switch Z-up or Y-up until the model stands correctly.

  4. 4

    Read the measurements

    Read the raw X × Y × Z bounding box, triangle count, file size and format, then compare the height with the sculptor's stated scale.

What an STL reader can tell me

Useful checks, honest limits

An STL contains only surface triangles. I can measure the geometry, count triangles and spot a missing limb or a support-only export. I cannot recover the original unit, a scale label, colour, material or print settings. If the bounding box disagrees with the listing, trust the measurement and investigate before printing.

Formats on this page

  • Supported: binary STL and ASCII STL.
  • Not supported: OBJ, FBX, STEP, STP, 3MF and other formats. Save as STL first.
  • Privacy: no upload, no account, no cookies, no stored model.

STL viewer questions I get asked

How do I open an STL file online?

Open this free STL viewer, choose your .stl file or drag it into the drop zone, and I parse it locally in your browser. You get a WebGL preview plus the bounding box, triangle count, file size and detected ASCII or binary format. Nothing is uploaded.

Is this a free STL viewer?

Yes. This STL viewer online is free and works without an account, cookie or upload. I built it as a quick check before a downloaded model reaches my Bambu Lab A1 Mini.

Can I view binary and ASCII STL files?

Yes. The STL file viewer detects binary STL from its triangle-count header and ASCII STL from its facet blocks, then renders both with WebGL. An STL reader only sees triangles — it cannot recover units, material or print settings.

Does this STL viewer upload my file?

No. The file is read with File.arrayBuffer() in your browser. I do not send it to a server, store it, or log it. Close the tab and the model is gone.

Why does my STL preview show the wrong size?

STL coordinates are unitless. I display the raw X × Y × Z values; your slicer usually treats them as millimetres. A file exported in inches or metres will look 25.4× smaller or 1000× larger until you scale it. Check the bounding box before you trust the number.

Can this open OBJ, FBX, STEP or STP files?

No. I have not added OBJ viewer, FBX viewer, STEP viewer, STP viewer or step file viewer online support here. This page reads STL only. Export your model as STL first if you only need the geometry preview.

What can I do after I preview the STL?

Use the height from the bounding box in the Miniature Scale Identifier to name the likely scale, then open the Slicer Percentage Calculator to convert it to the scale you print. The miniature size chart holds the full conversion matrix.

Keep checking the scale

A preview tells you the file is intact; it does not tell you the sculpt is the right size. After you note the height, use the miniature scale identifier and the slicer percentage calculator to finish the job. The full method is on the methodology page.
